patterns.title: Build, understand, vary
patterns.description: Carry a familiar object into one new capacity. Give the student a reason, an explanation, a construction and a variation.
patterns.caution: Keep the exact inherited files available. A passing program does not prove that the student understands it.

sources.title: Ada writing patterns and prose samples

nodes.label: Notice a difference
nodes.information: One observable change in the carried object.
nodes.instruction: Describe a difference the student can see in the current hall.
nodes.gain: A reason to investigate this operation.
nodes.bridge: What would have to change in our existing object?

nodes.label: Recall the inheritance
nodes.information: The previous lesson, its object and usable code.
nodes.instruction: Name the exact inherited file and what the student already knows; link rather than reprint.
nodes.gain: A clear boundary between inherited and new work.
nodes.bridge: Which part of that inheritance cannot yet do this?

nodes.label: Define the new part
nodes.information: The new concept and the conditions it needs.
nodes.instruction: Define the operation, then name what it does to the carried data.
nodes.gain: A usable account of the mechanism.
nodes.bridge: What happens to a small concrete input?

nodes.label: Trace a case
nodes.information: A small input, intermediate state and result.
nodes.instruction: Follow the data step by step; let the student predict the last step.
nodes.gain: A mental model for reading the code.
nodes.bridge: Where will these steps appear in the program?

nodes.label: Build and run
nodes.information: Complete new code, setup and execution.
nodes.job: Turn the explanation into a working object.
nodes.instruction: Introduce the code event, supply complete new code, then point out the important lines.
nodes.gain: A reconstructable example with named dependencies.
nodes.bridge: Does its behaviour match the trace?

nodes.label: Predict and vary
nodes.information: One meaningful change and its expected consequence.
nodes.instruction: Ask for a prediction before changing one relation. Run behavioural assertions and explain the result.
nodes.gain: A capacity to modify the example deliberately.
nodes.bridge: What can the next hall take as already available?

nodes.label: Carry onward
nodes.information: The object, code and capacity retained.
nodes.instruction: Name what is kept and the next problem it makes possible.
nodes.gain: A reason for the next lesson.
nodes.bridge: The next hall puts the retained capacity to work.

patterns.title: Leave the object, return changed
patterns.description: Follow one historical relation away from an object, then return to a detail whose meaning has changed.
patterns.caution: An excursion must change the encounter. History, critique and strangeness are choices, not required sections.

sources.title: Ada writing patterns and prose samples

nodes.label: Stay with a detail
nodes.information: A particular object, feature or resistance.
nodes.instruction: Let a visible detail hold the reader before it illustrates a thesis.
nodes.gain: Something specific to remember.
nodes.bridge: What about this detail makes leaving the room worthwhile?

nodes.label: Follow a history
nodes.information: One relevant person, practice or dispute.
nodes.instruction: Follow one sourced relation that answers the opening question.
nodes.gain: A context that matters to this object.
nodes.bridge: What distinction does this history make necessary?

nodes.label: Make a distinction
nodes.information: The formal relation needed for the stakes.
nodes.instruction: Explain only the formal distinction the passage now needs, with its conditions.
nodes.gain: A way to see the opening detail differently.
nodes.bridge: What happens when we apply this distinction here?

nodes.label: Return to the detail
nodes.information: The same object after the excursion.
nodes.instruction: Revisit the detail without recapping the whole journey.
nodes.gain: A changed relation to a familiar object.
nodes.bridge: Which possibility or constraint is newly visible?

nodes.label: Another possible use
nodes.information: A specific consequence or imagined extension.
nodes.instruction: Follow an alternative use far enough to have consequences. Identify invention as invention.
nodes.gain: A desire or question beyond the intended use.
nodes.bridge: What remains unresolved in that possibility?

nodes.label: Carry the question
nodes.information: The next encounter's pressure.
nodes.instruction: Let one unresolved relation move into the next hall.
nodes.gain: An invitation to keep reading.
nodes.bridge: The next object changes what this question can mean.

patterns.title: A claim meets resistance
patterns.description: Let a reasonable expectation meet a small discrepancy. Keep what the encounter actually establishes.
patterns.caution: The object need not be defective. Give the revised account something useful to do.

sources.title: Ada writing patterns and prose samples

nodes.label: Offer a claim
nodes.information: A plausible expectation about the artifact.
nodes.instruction: Name what a visitor could reasonably expect.
nodes.gain: A claim that can be investigated.
nodes.bridge: How could we encounter that expectation?

nodes.label: Try it
nodes.information: An action and its observable result.
nodes.instruction: Describe or perform one concrete trial.
nodes.gain: Evidence to compare with the expectation.
nodes.bridge: Which detail refuses to fit?

nodes.label: Stay with resistance
nodes.information: The discrepancy.
nodes.instruction: Allow the difference to be noticed before explaining it away.
nodes.gain: A more precise problem.
nodes.bridge: What condition could explain this result?

nodes.label: Name the boundary
nodes.information: The relevant definition or implementation limit.
nodes.instruction: Give the condition that accounts for the difference; avoid extending it to every algorithm.
nodes.gain: A defensible explanation.
nodes.bridge: What does the trial still establish?

nodes.label: Keep the finding
nodes.information: What remains true.
nodes.job: Preserve the value of the investigation.
nodes.instruction: State what we learned without abandoning the object.
nodes.gain: A smaller, stronger claim.
nodes.bridge: What new use benefits from that condition?

nodes.label: Try another relation
nodes.information: A variation or better question.
nodes.instruction: Develop a use that the revised account makes possible.
nodes.gain: A new direction for investigation.
nodes.bridge: Carry the finding into another encounter.

patterns.title: Bring the background forward
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation from an Ahmed reading
patterns.description: Stay with an ordinary object until the support it takes for granted becomes part of the encounter.
patterns.caution: This is our reusable route, not Ahmed's prose or a claim that her phenomenology is OOO.

nodes.label: An ordinary object
nodes.information: Something already present in the room.
nodes.instruction: Describe one thing without immediately giving it a symbolic job.
nodes.gain: A concrete point of attention.
nodes.bridge: What makes its apparent ordinariness possible?

nodes.label: Its usual work
nodes.information: How the object is normally used.
nodes.instruction: Describe a use and the relations it depends on.
nodes.gain: A view of the arrangement around it.
nodes.bridge: Which supporting relation has stayed unnoticed?

nodes.label: Notice the support
nodes.information: A surface, rule or placement previously backgrounded.
nodes.instruction: Bring one enabling condition into focus.
nodes.gain: A condition of the encounter.
nodes.bridge: What changes if that condition changes?

nodes.label: Turn the arrangement
nodes.information: A different approach, use or position.
nodes.instruction: Return to the object through the newly visible relation; mark imagined alterations.
nodes.gain: Another way of meeting the same object.
nodes.bridge: What can we now notice that the first description missed?

nodes.label: Stay with the change
nodes.information: A remaining difficulty or possibility.
nodes.instruction: Give the altered encounter time; it may be awkward, pleasurable or unresolved.
nodes.gain: A live relation rather than a closed verdict.
nodes.bridge: Let the next object develop this new attention.

patterns.title: Test an explanation in a situation
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation from an Ahmed reading
patterns.description: Introduce an explanation because a concrete difficulty needs it; return it to a situation that reveals its reach.
patterns.caution: A thinker is an interlocutor here. Verify the source and let the test remain fair.

nodes.label: A difficulty arises
nodes.information: Something that interrupts an ordinary encounter.
nodes.job: Give the concept a reason to enter.
nodes.instruction: Begin with the precise difficulty, not a general thesis.
nodes.gain: A question that needs an explanation.
nodes.bridge: Who or what offers an account of this?

nodes.label: An account enters
nodes.information: A sourced explanation or inherited concept.
nodes.instruction: Present the strongest relevant version with enough context to understand it.
nodes.gain: A possible way through the difficulty.
nodes.bridge: What does this account let us predict?

nodes.label: Its reach is tested
nodes.information: A detail the account may not settle.
nodes.instruction: Distinguish what the account establishes from what it leaves open.
nodes.gain: A narrower unresolved question.
nodes.bridge: What comparison could clarify the remaining issue?

nodes.label: Make it bodily
nodes.information: A concrete comparison in the museum.
nodes.instruction: Follow an action or change of position, attending to the result.
nodes.gain: An encounter the abstraction must answer to.
nodes.bridge: How must our account change after this?

nodes.label: Rework the concept
nodes.information: A revised distinction.
nodes.instruction: Use the comparison to refine the concept; keep its conditions visible.
nodes.gain: A more useful explanation.
nodes.bridge: What does the initial situation look like now?

nodes.label: Return to the difficulty
nodes.information: The opening scene seen again.
nodes.instruction: Return without merely repeating the opening question.
nodes.gain: A changed capacity to notice or act.
nodes.bridge: Carry the remaining problem onward.

patterns.title: Let a word change its force
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation from an Ahmed reading
patterns.description: Follow a word through material situations until it acquires another consequence.
patterns.caution: A word's resemblance is not evidence that two mechanisms are the same. Keep their differences visible.

nodes.label: A word in use
nodes.information: A word attached to a current object or action.
nodes.instruction: Choose a word whose meaning matters to this encounter.
nodes.gain: A term with material consequences.
nodes.bridge: What does this word ask someone or something to do?

nodes.label: Give it a situation
nodes.information: The action or arrangement the word names.
nodes.instruction: Describe a particular interaction without stretching the technical definition.
nodes.gain: A connection between word and action.
nodes.bridge: What happens when this action is repeated?

nodes.label: Follow repetition
nodes.information: A relation sustained over time.
nodes.instruction: Trace what repeated actions make easier, harder or expected.
nodes.gain: An understanding of how the situation persists.
nodes.bridge: Who or what is committed to continuing it?

nodes.label: Meet its pressure
nodes.information: The cost, demand or limit in this case.
nodes.instruction: Locate the pressure in the specific arrangement, avoiding a universal moral.
nodes.gain: A consequential choice to examine.
nodes.bridge: Can this same word serve another relation?

nodes.label: Let it turn
nodes.information: A different use of the word and object.
nodes.instruction: Find a concrete use that changes the term's force; name differences between mechanisms.
nodes.gain: An alternative that cannot be reduced to the first reading.
nodes.bridge: Leave this possibility available for a later encounter.

patterns.title: From an odd beginning to a build
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation from The Nature of Code reading
patterns.description: Use a surprising historical object to invite a student into one well-bounded construction.
patterns.caution: Keep the opening short. The student still needs prerequisites, definitions and executable new code.

sources.title: The Nature of Code · Randomness, opening paragraphs

nodes.label: An unusual beginning
nodes.information: One sourced historical object or practice.
nodes.instruction: Introduce a small historical puzzle relevant to the operation.
nodes.gain: A reason to care about the topic.
nodes.bridge: What can we do with this problem now?

nodes.label: A present possibility
nodes.information: The capacity available in the museum.
nodes.instruction: Connect the opening to one object we can build on.
nodes.gain: A clear destination for this lesson.
nodes.bridge: What do we already have that can support it?

nodes.label: Name the starting point
nodes.information: Inherited objects, code and knowledge.
nodes.instruction: Link the exact previous lesson and name any new prerequisite.
nodes.gain: A reliable starting state.
nodes.bridge: How can the new problem be represented simply?

nodes.label: Experience becomes a rule
nodes.information: A small model and its representation.
nodes.instruction: Work through one example before presenting its implementation.
nodes.gain: A rule the student can explain.
nodes.bridge: Which operations will execute that rule?

nodes.label: Construct the example
nodes.information: New code, setup and a check.
nodes.instruction: Supply complete new code and necessary setup, then run it.
nodes.gain: A working example tied to the rule.
nodes.bridge: What change would demonstrate understanding?

nodes.label: Vary and carry
nodes.information: A prediction, a variation and retained state.
nodes.instruction: Change one relation, test it, then name what travels onward.
nodes.gain: A reusable capacity.
nodes.bridge: The next lesson uses this state.

patterns.title: Follow code into culture
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation from the 10 PRINT reading
patterns.description: Let a small technical detail open a cultural relation, then bring that relation back to the specific mechanism.
patterns.caution: Choose one excursion per passage. A chapter-length source is not a one-hall word budget.

nodes.label: A small operation
nodes.information: One specific operation in an artifact.
nodes.instruction: Start with a detail small enough to retain through an excursion.
nodes.gain: A concrete technical object.
nodes.bridge: Where else has this operation or word mattered?

nodes.label: An unexpected relation
nodes.information: One relevant historical or cultural practice.
nodes.instruction: Follow a verified relation without treating resemblance as identity.
nodes.gain: Another context for the object.
nodes.bridge: Which distinction is needed to connect these contexts?

nodes.label: Name the difference
nodes.information: The categories or formal relation at stake.
nodes.instruction: Define the distinction that prevents an easy analogy.
nodes.gain: A way to compare without collapsing the cases.
nodes.bridge: Where are the consequences of that distinction felt?

nodes.label: Give the stakes a scene
nodes.information: A particular event, use or conflict.
nodes.instruction: Describe the stakes through a sourced case or clearly marked invention.
nodes.gain: A felt reason for the comparison.
nodes.bridge: How does this change the opening operation?

nodes.label: Return to the mechanism
nodes.information: The initial operation in its new context.
nodes.instruction: Revisit the detail, showing what the other context made visible.
nodes.gain: A changed relation to the algorithm.
nodes.bridge: What tension should remain unresolved?

nodes.label: Hold two consequences
nodes.information: A pleasure and a difficulty that coexist.
nodes.instruction: Let both consequences remain specific; avoid a universal verdict.
nodes.gain: A reason to continue thinking or making.
nodes.bridge: Carry that tension into the next encounter.

patterns.title: Spiral outward from one object
patterns.description: Widen the scale of attention while keeping a specific object in view.
patterns.caution: Each widening needs evidence and a bridge. Scale alone does not make a passage profound.
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation of an Ada Writer preset; no source passage recorded for the preset

sources.title: Ada Writer: presets, harvesting and provenance

nodes.label: Attend to a detail
nodes.information: One observed property
nodes.job: Give attention a place to begin
nodes.instruction: Describe a small detail of the actual artifact that matters to the subject.
nodes.gain: An object to follow
nodes.bridge: What makes this detail possible?

nodes.label: Find its conditions
nodes.information: Mechanism and setting
nodes.instruction: Follow the detail into its immediate conditions, naming what the map actually does.
nodes.gain: A mechanism behind the appearance
nodes.bridge: Where did that arrangement come from?

nodes.label: Widen into history
nodes.information: A sourced historical decision
nodes.instruction: Choose one historical episode that changes how the detail reads; explain the connection.
nodes.gain: A reason this could have been otherwise
nodes.bridge: What did that choice enable or exclude?

nodes.label: Press a consequence
nodes.information: A limit or overlooked use
nodes.instruction: Trace one concrete consequence without treating the artifact as proof of a whole social theory.
nodes.gain: A consequential distinction
nodes.bridge: What can we now notice or try?

nodes.label: Return at another scale
nodes.information: The original detail reconsidered
nodes.instruction: Return to the same detail with a new question or possible use.
nodes.gain: A changed way of attending
nodes.bridge: Carry this question to the next encounter.

patterns.title: Braid the room with another thread
patterns.description: Alternate two strands so each return changes the other.
patterns.caution: Track each strand clearly. A historical name or theory must do work when it returns.
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation of an Ada Writer preset; no source passage recorded for the preset

sources.title: Ada Writer: presets, harvesting and provenance

nodes.label: Room A: an unfinished encounter
nodes.information: A present event
nodes.instruction: Begin an encounter in the hall and leave a precise question unresolved.
nodes.gain: A reason to follow a second thread
nodes.bridge: Which other encounter speaks to this question?

nodes.label: History B: another situation
nodes.information: One sourced episode
nodes.instruction: Enter a historical situation with its own stakes; identify its relation to the hall.
nodes.gain: Another way to understand the problem
nodes.bridge: What does this make visible in our room?

nodes.label: Room A: test the relation
nodes.information: A return to the artifact
nodes.instruction: Describe what the artifact supports and where it differs from the historical case.
nodes.gain: A bounded comparison
nodes.bridge: Does this also change our reading of the history?

nodes.label: History B: revise the reading
nodes.information: A complication in that episode
nodes.instruction: Revisit the historical case with the distinction the artifact has sharpened.
nodes.gain: A history that resists a simple moral
nodes.bridge: What can travel back without flattening that difference?

nodes.label: Crossing: a changed encounter
nodes.information: Both strands held together
nodes.instruction: Return to the room with a new action or unresolved tension.
nodes.gain: A relation neither strand supplied alone
nodes.bridge: Let the next hall put this relation under pressure.

patterns.title: Begin with the consequence
patterns.description: Start inside an event, then reconstruct what made it possible.
patterns.caution: Use an observed or explicitly proposed event. Reconstruction must not invent a cause.
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation of an Ada Writer preset; no source passage recorded for the preset

sources.title: Ada Writer: presets, harvesting and provenance

nodes.label: The event is already happening
nodes.information: A specific consequence
nodes.instruction: Place the reader inside one visible event before explaining its machinery.
nodes.gain: Something worth understanding
nodes.bridge: How did this become possible?

nodes.label: Reconstruct the conditions
nodes.information: Earlier state and actions
nodes.instruction: Work backward through known conditions; distinguish observation from inference.
nodes.gain: A traceable history
nodes.bridge: Which operation links these conditions to this result?

nodes.label: Name the mechanism
nodes.information: The operative relation
nodes.instruction: Define the mechanism and explain the relevant interaction.
nodes.gain: An explanation that fits the event
nodes.bridge: What if one condition changed?

nodes.label: Try a counterfactual
nodes.information: One changed condition
nodes.instruction: Choose a variation the artifact permits; say whether it was observed or remains to test.
nodes.gain: A limit on the causal claim
nodes.bridge: What can we do when the event happens again?

nodes.label: Return to the event
nodes.information: Consequence with understanding
nodes.instruction: Re-enter the event, allowing intention and outcome to remain different.
nodes.gain: A capacity to notice and respond
nodes.bridge: Carry a testable question onward.

patterns.title: Let a mechanism become necessary
patterns.description: Let observations accumulate before naming the mechanism they require.
patterns.caution: Use in reflective passages. Never delay setup or prerequisites needed to complete a tutorial.
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation of an Ada Writer preset; no source passage recorded for the preset

sources.title: Ada Writer: presets, harvesting and provenance

nodes.label: Encounter without its label
nodes.information: An observable event
nodes.instruction: Let the reader notice a relation before supplying its technical name.
nodes.gain: A concrete puzzle
nodes.bridge: What happens when the condition changes?

nodes.label: Gather a second clue
nodes.information: A contrasting observation
nodes.instruction: Add one observation that changes the first rather than repeating it.
nodes.gain: Evidence for a possible explanation
nodes.bridge: Which explanation fits both encounters?

nodes.label: Try an interpretation
nodes.information: A plausible account and its limit
nodes.instruction: Offer a provisional explanation; test it against a detail it cannot explain.
nodes.gain: A reason for greater precision
nodes.bridge: What distinction is missing?

nodes.label: Name what the clues require
nodes.information: A definition and its conditions
nodes.instruction: Introduce the concept where it becomes useful, then connect it to each clue.
nodes.gain: A concept attached to experience
nodes.bridge: How does this name alter the first encounter?

nodes.label: Return and vary
nodes.information: A new use of the explanation
nodes.instruction: Revisit the initial event and propose a meaningful variation.
nodes.gain: A way to explore beyond recognition
nodes.bridge: Carry the variation to the next lesson.

patterns.title: Return to the object with a difference
patterns.description: Let a familiar object or gesture recur under changed conditions.
patterns.caution: Every recurrence needs a change. A repeated motif is not proof of continuity in the code.
patterns.origin: Ada adaptation of an Ada Writer preset; no source passage recorded for the preset

sources.title: Ada Writer: presets, harvesting and provenance

nodes.label: Recognise the carried object
nodes.information: An object and its actual lineage
nodes.instruction: Name what persists from earlier halls: appearance, code, data or a gesture.
nodes.gain: A precise continuity
nodes.bridge: Which condition has changed here?

nodes.label: First variation
nodes.information: One new relation
nodes.instruction: Describe the object's changed behaviour and what produces it.
nodes.gain: A difference within the familiar
nodes.bridge: What stays constant if something else changes?

nodes.label: Return to a stable feature
nodes.information: What really remained invariant
nodes.instruction: Check the claim of sameness against the original feature.
nodes.gain: A baseline for comparison
nodes.bridge: Where does this continuity reach its limit?

nodes.label: Second variation, new stakes
nodes.information: A further transformation
nodes.instruction: Change one relation that alters what the object allows; explain a consequence.
nodes.gain: A new question about its use
nodes.bridge: Does the old name still help us understand it?

nodes.label: Recognise it differently
nodes.information: The motif after both variations
nodes.instruction: Return to the object without forcing a final identity or moral.
nodes.gain: A way to follow continuity through change
nodes.bridge: Name what the next hall inherits.
